t: In front of you is the National Gallery, on Trafalgar Square. It's an art museum founded in 1824, and it holds more than 2,300 paintings, dating from the mid-13th century to 1900. The building was designed by William Wilkins, an architect and classical scholar who also designed Downing College, Cambridge, and University College London. Sir George Beaumont, an art patron and amateur painter, matters here because his was the first bequest of paintings to the gallery. He played a crucial part in its creation. The current director is Gabriele Finaldi.
